office_does: One of 49 Washington State Senators, serving a four-year term writing state law, budgets and taxes for the 43rd District (Capitol Hill, University District, Wallingford, Fremont, Eastlake and downtown Seattle).
race_blurb: Two Democrats: Senate Majority Leader Jamie Pedersen, prime sponsor of the 2026 millionaires tax that I-645 would repeal, faces labor communicator Hannah Sabio-Howell, who runs to his left and refuses corporate PAC money. KUOW reports Pedersen took about 66% in the primary to her 23%.

candidates.summary: Senate Majority Leader, in the Legislature since 2007 and general counsel at McKinstry; prime sponsor of the 2026 tax on household income over $1 million.
highlights: Led passage of the Millionaires Tax and a capital gains tax, paired with tax cuts for working families [S1][S11]
Cites banning masked ICE agents and limiting camera surveillance for immigration enforcement [S1]
Leads on marriage equality, LGBTQ+ civil rights and transgender privacy protections; cites abortion rights [S1]
Says he worked to 'defend the Climate Commitment Act' and backed $100 million for police hiring and training [S4]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025); defended the millionaires tax against the repeal effort [S10][S7]

taxes.basis: Prime sponsor of the millionaires tax and the capital gains tax, but paired with tax cuts, with openness to estate-tax rollback and opposition to a payroll-tax fund.

spending.basis: Commits to 'amply funding schools' and cites $1.4 billion more for school districts and $770 million for housing.

housing.basis: Voted for 2025 rent stabilization and cites housing funding, alongside laws streamlining housing construction.

safety.basis: Supported a $100 million police hiring and training investment, alongside license-revocation reform for misconduct.

climate.basis: Says he worked to defend the Climate Commitment Act; cites climate action among accomplishments.

experience.basis: In the Legislature since 2007, Senate Majority Leader, with an enacted signature tax law.

local-control.basis: Voted for ESHB 2266, a state requirement that cities allow supportive housing and shelters in specified zones.

reform.basis: Frames his approach as coalition-building; accepts institutional and union backing and holds a large fundraising lead, against a no-corporate-PAC opponent.

immigration.basis: Cites enacted bans on masked ICE agents and on camera surveillance for immigration enforcement.

social.basis: Long record leading on marriage equality, LGBTQ+ civil rights and transgender privacy; cites abortion rights and Planned Parenthood funding.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yea on ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parents' rights law; no statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: Former Working Washington communications director and legislative staffer, making a first run for office; wants new corporate and payroll taxes, universal pre-K and non-police crisis response, and refuses corporate PAC money.
highlights: Calls the millionaires tax 'a super important first step'; wants a corporate income tax and a payroll-based Well Washington Fund [S4][S5][S6]
Proposes social workers on non-violent emergency calls and alternatives to incarceration [S4]
'The only campaign in this race not taking corporate PAC money' [S1]
Would restrict AI and surveillance use by law enforcement, 'including the expansion of data centers' [S4]
No public position found on the three initiatives [S3][S4][S5]

taxes.basis: Wants a corporate income tax, a payroll-based fund and reversal of tax cuts for the ultra-wealthy, beyond the millionaires tax.

spending.basis: Proposes universal pre-K, a home-care cash benefit, restored childcare enrollment and social housing investment.

housing.basis: Social housing investment and a tighter rent cap, paired with statewide supply deregulation ('ending apartment bans', cutting red tape).

safety.basis: Non-police responders for non-violent calls, community programs as alternatives to incarceration, restoring use-of-force standards.

experience.basis: No elected office; runs against 'career politicians who protect the status quo'.

local-control.basis: Wants to end apartment bans statewide and build housing 'everywhere', plus a tighter statewide rent cap.

reform.basis: Refuses corporate PAC money, frames the race against corporate deal-making, and supports even-year local elections.

immigration.basis: Would shield data from immigration enforcement, strip incentives from ICE contractors and bar hiring former ICE officers.

healthcare.basis: Supports the state backstopping federal cuts and taking steps toward universal healthcare.

social.basis: Serves on the Pro-Choice Washington PAC board 'to advance reproductive justice'; organized with queer rights organizations.

tech.basis: Would regulate and restrict AI and surveillance use by law enforcement, including the expansion of data centers.
